slot_note: Forecasting block, second build of the wave; seed FC04 (station maturity ramp) not used: its forward-maturity driver repeats the age-forward structure of task132 drawn the same day, so the slot keeps the objective and draws a fresh world
niche: a non-bank consumer lender's quarter-end expected credit loss allowance on its unsecured personal loan book, built from the model team's cumulative default curve by months on book, the staging rule and the scenario weights
layer1: a loan book extract with origination and first-repayment dates rather than months on book
a hardship register joined by loan number, with arrangements that start, end and are cancelled
behaviour scores at origination and now on different scorecard versions with a mapping table
a default curve file with one curve per product and a model version stamp
scenario multipliers and weights in a committee-approved workbook
an outcomes history the model was developed on, which the allowance does not use
stakeholder_role: head of credit risk reporting at a consumer lender, who presents the quarter-end ECL allowance to the Audit and Risk Committee

spine.entity: one performing unsecured personal loan at the reporting date

world.org_type: non-bank consumer lender with an unsecured personal loan book

driver: A cumulative outcome curve is filed from each unit's entry, and every unit in scope has already survived part of it, so its forward probability is the curve's remaining increments divided by its own survival to date; reading the curve from entry for every unit overstates the total, and shifting it to the unit's age without the division understates it.
driver_concrete: The model team's cumulative PD curve runs from origination by repayments fallen due, so a performing loan at month a carries marginal PDs (C(a+k) - C(a+k-1)) / (1 - C(a)); reading the curve from month 1 for every loan's remaining term books about 43 per cent too much, and shifting it by months on book without the survival division books about 3 per cent too little.
stump: A competent solver applies the cumulative PD curve to each loan's remaining months counted from the reporting date as if it were a term structure and books an allowance about 43 per cent high; the step that lands it there is reading a curve indexed by months on book as if every performing loan were new.

differentiation.task132: task132 forecasts failures of replaceable modules in which a failed unit is renewed by a new one at age zero, so the forecast weights each band by the present module's survival and adds its replacement; here a loan defaults once and is not replaced, and the construction is the conditional increment of a filed curve for loans that have already survived part of it.
differentiation.task130: task130 runs a closed group off a rationed list; here nothing is rationed and no group closes: each loan's forward loss is a survival-conditioned share of a filed curve.

notes: Forcing event: the 30 September 2026 quarter close. Gate G forecasting repeats task132 by design: both builds sit in the Forecasting block; the mechanisms differ (task132 replacement of failed modules in a spares forecast, task133 conditioning a lifetime curve on survival to date). Realism rebuild 2026-10-11 moved the allowance to AUD 13,667,000 with realistic default levels.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who cleans the book and reads CRM-ECL-04 3.2 and the curve header correctly takes the curve's increments from each loan's months on book as its forward monthly PDs without dividing by the loan's survival to the reporting date, and books about AUD 13.32 million against AUD 13,773,000.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each loan's AASB 9 12-month or lifetime expected credit loss from a cumulative default curve by months on book, staged, scenario-weighted, re-amortised and discounted; with another field's nouns the staging triggers, LGD, EAD and coverage ratios have nothing to attach to, so the task does not read the same.
